q: 1. The moment of resistance developed in a beam subjected to bending moment will, at any instant be
explain: For static equilibrium in a beam, the internal moment of resistance developed by the stresses in the cross-section must exactly balance the external bending moment applied at 그 section.

q: 2. A simply supported beam is subjected to a central concentrated load. The slope at the two ends is given by
explain: For a simply supported beam with a central load W, the maximum slope (θ) at the supports is WL² / 16EI.

q: 3. A simply supported beam of span L carries a concentrated load W at its mid-span. The maximum bending moment M is
explain: The maximum bending moment for a central point load on a simply supported beam occurs at the center and is equal to WL/4.

q: 4. Maximum deflection of a cantilever due to pure bending moment M at its free end, is
explain: Using the moment-area method, the deflection at the free end for a constant moment M is ML² / 2EI.

q: 5. The maximum deflection of a cantilever beam of length l with a point load W at the free end is
explain: The standard formula for maximum deflection at the free end of a cantilever with a point load is Wl³ / 3EI.

q: 6. A beam encastered at both the ends is called
explain: A fixed beam (also known as a built-in or encastered beam) has both ends restrained against rotation and displacement.

q: 7. The shear force of a cantilever beam of length l carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length is... at the fixed end.
explain: The total load on the beam is w * l. To maintain equilibrium, the vertical reaction (Shear Force) at the fixed end must equal the total load.

q: 8. The bending moment of a cantilever beam of length l and carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length is... at the free end.
explain: As per the definition of Bending Moment, the sum of moments of forces to the right of the free end is zero.

q: 9. The shear force in the centre of a simply supported beam carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length, is
explain: For a symmetrical UDL on an SS beam, the SF diagram passes through zero at the mid-span.

q: 10. When there is a sudden increase or decrease in shear force diagram between any two points, it indicates that there is a
options: point load at the two points
no loading between the two points
uniformly distributed load between the two points
uniformly varying load between the two points
explain: A vertical jump in the shear force diagram always corresponds to the application of a concentrated (point) load at 그 point.

q: 11. A simply supported beam carrying a UDL... is propped at the centre... The reaction of the prop will be
explain: By equating the downward deflection of a SS beam due to UDL (5wL⁴/384EI) to the upward deflection due to the prop (PL³/48EI), the prop reaction is found to be 5/8 of the total load W.

q: 12. The slope of curve of B.M. diagram at any section will be equal to
options: the slope of moment at that section
the slope of S.F. diagram at that section
the ordinate of S.F. diagram at that section
the area of S.F. diagram starting from any one end
explain: The rate of change of bending moment (dM/dx) at a section is equal to the shear force (V) at that section.

q: 13. Which of the following beams will have points of contraflexure? (self weight is negligible)
options: a simply supported beam with udl over entire span
a overhanging beam with loading only over supported span and not on overhangs
fixed beam subjected to concentrated load
cantilever subjected to uniformly varying loads
explain: Fixed beams develop hogging moments at the supports and sagging moments in the center, necessitating points of contraflexure where the BM is zero.

q: 14. In a three hinged arch, the bending moment will be zero
options: at both right and left hinges
explain: By definition, a hinge cannot resist or transfer bending moment; therefore, the BM is zero at every hinge location.

q: 15. In a simple bending of beams, the stress in the beam varies
explain: According to the flexure formula (σ = My/I), the bending stress is directly proportional to the distance from the neutral axis, resulting in a linear distribution.

q: 16. When a beam is subjected to bending moment, the stress at any point is ............ the distance of the point from the neutral axis.
explain: As per the flexure formula σ = (M/I)y, for a given section, stress increases linearly as you move further away from the neutral axis.

q: 17. If the depth is kept constant for a beam of uniform strength, then its width will vary in proportional to
explain: σ = M / (bd²/6). If σ and d are constant, then b must be directly proportional to M (b ∝ M).

q: 18. A beam of uniform strength has
options: same bending stress at every section
same bending moment at every section
same shear stress at every section
explain: The core definition of a beam of uniform strength is that the maximum fiber stress is constant across every cross-section along its longitudinal axis.

q: 19. The maximum shear stress developed in a beam of rectangular section is ............ the average shear stress.
explain: For a rectangular section, the shear stress distribution is parabolic, and the maximum shear stress (at the neutral axis) is exactly 1.5 times the average shear stress (τ_max = 1.5 * V/A).

q: 20. The product E.I. is called
explain: Flexural rigidity (EI) represents the resistance of a beam section to bending deformation.

q: 21. Polar moment of inertia of a circular section with radius R is ............
explain: For a circle, $J = \frac{\pi D^4}{32}$. Since $D=2R$, $J = \frac{\pi (2R)^4}{32} = \frac{16\pi R^4}{32} = \frac{\pi R^4}{2}$.

q: 22. Find the maximum BM induced in a cantilever beam subjected to a point load of 10 KN. Length of beam is 10 m. The load is located at a distance of 3 m from the free end:-
explain: Distance from the fixed end = 10 − 3 = 7 m. M = 10 × 7 = 70 kN-m.

q: 23. Maximum bending moment occurs at the centre if the simply supported beam is subjected to
options: uniformly distributed load throughout the span
triangular load with maximum intensity at centre
explain: All three symmetric loading patterns produce maximum BM at mid-span for a simply supported beam.

q: 24. Maximum bending moment occurs where
options: shear force is less than one
explain: Since V=dM/dx, M is at an extremum (max/min) where V=0, i.e. where the shear force diagram crosses zero and changes sign.

q: 25. In a beam where shear force is maximum the bending moment will be
explain: As per the answer key; there's no fixed universal relation between the location of max SF and the BM value there — it depends on the specific loading case.

q: 26. The bending moment diagram for a cantilever beam subjected to a moment at the end of the beam would be
explain: A pure end moment with no other loads produces a constant BM throughout — a rectangle.

q: 27. A beam simply supported at ends is subjected to load. The maximum bending moment is located where
explain: Since dM/dx = V, BM is maximum/minimum exactly where V = 0.

q: 28. In a continuous beam, the point where bending moment changes sign is called
explain: All three terms describe the same location where BM sign reverses.

q: 29. In a fixed beam, the points of contraflexure,
options: for a moment applied load are 2
explain: Fixed beams develop two points of contraflexure for each of these standard load cases.

q: 30. The critical bending moment caused in a fixed end beam loaded with a uniformly distributed load (W=wL) throughout is
explain: For a fixed-fixed beam under UDL, the fixed-end (support) moment = WL/12.

q: 31. In a simply supported beam with span (L) having a triangular load with its intensity 0 at both ends and W at center. The maximum BM will be
explain: As per the answer key for this symmetric triangular loading case.

q: 32. A beam of uniform strength will have at every cross-section the same
explain: A beam of uniform strength is designed so bending stress remains constant at every section, by varying the section dimensions.

q: 33. The expression EI d⁴y/dx⁴ at any section for a beam is equal to
explain: Differentiating the beam equation twice more: EI·d⁴y/dx⁴ = w, the load intensity.

q: 34. Find the value of thrust, if the member (beam) is subjected to an inclined force having magnitude 5 kN and inclination with vertical is 30°
explain: Thrust (component along the horizontal beam axis) = 5 × sin30° = 2.5 kN.

q: 35. Which of the following end conditions permits the displacement in any direction and also rotation?
explain: A free end has no restraint at all — it permits both translation and rotation.

q: 36. A beam is supported over three rollers lying in the same plane. The beam is stable for
options: loading with no component in the direction of the beam
loading with no component perpendicular to the direction of beam
only when no load except self weight acts
explain: Three rollers alone provide no horizontal restraint and are generally unstable except under special/self-weight-only loading conditions.

q: 37. The shear force in a concrete beam is assumed to act
options: on a plane normal to the longitudinal axis
explain: Transverse shear force acts perpendicular to the beam's longitudinal axis.

q: 38. Rate of change of bending moment is equal to
explain: dM/dx = V — the fundamental beam relation between bending moment and shear force.

q: 39. A Prismatic bar when subjected to pure bending assumes the shape of
explain: Under pure (constant) bending moment, a prismatic bar bends into a circular arc of constant curvature.

q: 40. Load required to produce unit deflection is called
explain: Stiffness = load / deflection, i.e. the load needed to produce one unit of deflection.

q: 41. A cantilever beam is one which is:
options: Fixed at one end and free at other end
Supported on more than two supports
explain: A cantilever has one fully fixed end and one completely free end.

q: 42. If the shear force along a section of a beam is zero, the bending moment at the section is:
explain: Since dM/dx = V, wherever shear force is zero, bending moment reaches a local extremum — commonly the maximum bending moment for typical loading cases.
